a3046.speech: said poultry farming is one of the livestock segments that contributes most to covering the animal protein deficit, food security, income generation and employment in the country ; "As a result of government incentives for private investment (hatcheries, feed factories, slaughterhouses), and the integration of small and medium-sized producers into the maize and soya production chain, the sector achieved substantial results, reaching national production last year of about 135,000 tonnes of chicken and 29.8 million dozen eggs" ; "For us, the poultry sector is a very important sector within our development pillar; it is a priority to do everything possible for Mozambique to reach full food self-sufficiency in this protein - less than 20 per cent of our market is supplied by imported chicken" ; "We see this meeting as a unique opportunity to strengthen partnerships between government, the private sector, academia and international partners, aligned around a vision of modern, sustainable and inclusive poultry farming" ; explained that poultry farming contributes to the supply of affordable animal protein, employment opportunities for young people and women, and the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises along the value chain, from production to processing and marketing ; "This subsector continues to face challenges regarding the availability of inputs and quality inputs, including the quality of day-old chicks, as well as access to sustainable markets" ; "From January to September of this year, 21,800 tonnes of chicken and 5.4 million dozen eggs were imported."

a3046.speaker: Rafael Estevao, National Director of Livestock, Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries
a3046.speech: said one of the factors why poultry farming is not developing at an astronomical speed is that most of the raw materials, soya and maize, used to produce feed are imported from outside the country ; "As a country we are able to increase maize production to satisfy [demand and reduce] the volume of imports considerably; we are closer to self-sufficiency than before."

a3343.speaker: Obert Jiri, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development of Zimbabwe
a3343.speech: Said there has been significant growth in the horticulture sector, with blueberries recording a 7 percent increase and pecan nuts achieving a 12 percent rise. ; "The growth has led to substantial exports with pecan nuts reaching 1 100 metric tons and blue berry 8 500 metric tones of high-quality produce."

a3343.speaker: Obert Jiri, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development of Zimbabwe
a3343.speech: Said the Zimbabwe Horticulture Recovery and Growth Plan is set for review for the period 2026-2030, focusing on building on growth areas, that is concentrating on sectors that have shown growth and re-evaluating areas that had not performed.

a3343.speaker: An official (unnamed)
a3343.speech: Said on Thursday that the horticulture sector in Zimbabwe is poised for major growth as the country targets to create a US$2 billion industry by 2030.

a3412.speaker: Hon. Lukaezi, regional councillor for Sibbinda constituency
a3412.speech: At one point presented the burning issue of the predicament of maize farmers in the Zambezi in their meetings in Katima Mulilo; it seems the results and response to such discussion have not borne many visible fruits.

a3532.speaker: Sources close to Saint George club (anonymous)
a3532.speech: According to sources close to the club, the Portuguese Head Coach Carlos Pinto, a huge fan of team work, might not be happy with Salahadin’s individual attitude and, having a number of options in attack, he may not give him a regular place if he couldn’t make it at the start of the season.

a3532.speaker: Salhadin Said, Ethiopian international striker
a3532.speech: “I am in good condition and in less than three weeks I will be ready for real action,” Salhadin told reporters.

a3532.speaker: A coach who watched the team in friendly matches (anonymous)
a3532.speech: “I am waiting to watch the pairing of Aschalew Girma and Edwin Frempong in Central defense,” a coach who watched the team in friendly matches remarked.

a3568.speaker: Government of Morocco (proposal)
a3568.speech: Shortly after the creation of the AES on 16 September 2023, attention was drawn to the Moroccan proposal to open its maritime frontage to the three countries on the way to confederation.

a3581.speaker: Antoine de Saint-Exupery (quoted in the obituary)
a3581.speech: "He who has gone, so we but cherish his memory, abides with us, more potent, nay, more present than the living man."

a3758.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a3758.speech: Together with his deputy JD Vance, berated Zelenskyy, telling him he has no respect and has never said thank you even though America has given huge sums of money under Joe Biden's administration to support the war between Ukraine and Russia ; told Zelenskyy that he has no power to dictate what he wants because the war Putin is waging on his country has become dire and there is no prospect of him winning it without America's help ; went on to warn Zelenskyy that the stubbornness he is showing does not benefit him because what he is doing is stoking a third world war ; told Zelenskyy that it is clear he is not ready for Russia and Ukraine to be at peace, and that if he wants that he should come back to America when he is ready for the two countries to talk so that the war can end.

a3758.speaker: Donald Trump and JD Vance, US President and Vice-President
a3758.speech: Told Zelenskyy: “You are a brutal leader and you should be tried for atrocities against your own people. You are also disrespectful, especially towards us Americans, so go away, and when you are ready, come back, do not waste our time” ; Trump went on to tell Zelenskyy: “Sign right there, we are not helping you any more.”

a3758.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, President of Ukraine
a3758.speech: Answered back and told Vance: “What kind of respect is it that you want us to give to your country? Since this war began, we have been on our own, so what are you saying to us? What kind of respect is that?” ; refused outright to sign the agreement with America over their minerals, saying it was unwise to enter into an agreement that offered no vision showing that Russia would not start a war with Ukraine again.

a3794.speaker: Swissinfo.ch (report)
a3794.speech: Reported that the Federal Council, Switzerland's executive body, was notified of the cuts to international cooperation on Wednesday last week, which has only affected three countries, including Zambia ; "As a result, the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) will end its bilateral development programmes with Albania, Bangladesh and Zambia by the end of 2028."

a3794.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a3794.speech: Say that there are concerns that the Switzerland bilateral aid cut to the three countries is as a result of poor governance issues, including human rights violations.

a3831.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) Results Report 2024
a3831.speech: Shows progress on global health goals, even in times of growing financial uncertainties ; presents a mid-term assessment of WHO’s performance in implementing the Programme budget 2024–2025 and highlights WHO’s work in over 150 countries ; shows significant progress on coverage with essential health services, protection from health emergencies, and enjoyment of healthier lives, but that progress is insufficient to reach the health-related Sustainable Development Goals by 2030 — an estimated 431 million more people covered with essential health services without catastrophic health spending, an estimated 637 million more people better protected from health emergencies, and 1.4 billion more people living with better health and well-being.

a3831.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a3831.speech: “This report shows how, with WHO’s support, many countries are making progress on a huge range of health indicators, helping their populations to live healthier lives, giving them greater access to essential health services, and keeping them safer against health emergencies. In a world of multiple overlapping challenges and constrained resources for global health, these results demonstrate why the world needs a strong and sustainably-financed WHO, delivering the high-quality, trusted support on which countries and their people rely.”

a3831.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3831.speech: Recognizes the sustained commitment of Member States and says it will work with new and existing donors and partners to secure additional funding, with securing predictable, sustainable and resilient financing the key objective of the Investment Round, which has mobilized over US$ 1.7 billion in pledges from 71 contributors, covering 53% of WHO’s voluntary funding needs.

a3913.speaker: Ahmed Ali Dimbio, President of the "Climate and Development Network" Association of Djibouti (RC&D-D)
a3913.speech: Welcomes the partnership his association has with UNDP to fight insalubrity and help improve the living environment of the population: "Without UNDP's support, it would have been difficult for us to carry out the noble actions we are undertaking" ; thanks the UN organisation for the tireless efforts it deploys in the fight against the effects of climate change ; specified that the environment question is everyone's business and that efforts must be united and converge in the same direction in order to win the fight against poor household-waste management.

a3913.speaker: Fatima El Sheikh, UNDP Resident Representative in Djibouti
a3913.speech: "Climate change and sustainability are everyone's business. COVID-19 taught us a lesson about our relationship with our planet and about the way we maintain it. If we do not loosen our grip on nature, this will not be the last crisis. We must be innovative and adopt a different approach to ensure a green and sustainable socio-economic recovery. Each of us has a role to play and can make a difference."

a3913.speaker: Fatima El Sheikh, UNDP Resident Representative in Djibouti
a3913.speech: Congratulated the initiative of civil society and of the young Djiboutians who created their own network with a view to working on climate-resilient local and national development; said UNDP is determined to support them in this approach and that she is convinced that if we join forces, we will be able to ensure a green and sustainable recovery that will allow us to secure a better future for all.

a3953.speaker: Maria Zakharova, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman
a3953.speech: In her weekly media briefing July 23, criticized United States support for educational programs, media and NGOs in Africa, saying “the allocation of grants fits into the White House’s efforts to promote the idea that there is…”

a3953.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a3953.speech: Has praised the entire healthcare system, and particularly the hard-working team of scientists and specialists from different institutions for their efforts at research and creating a series of coronavirus vaccines for use against the coronavirus both at home and abroad.

a3977.speaker: National Institute of Statistics (INE) (data release)
a3977.speech: According to the INE, on the demand side growth was driven mainly by final consumption expenditure of households, up 13.8%, and by exports, which rose sharply by 78.9%, while investment fell 10.3% and public administration and non-profit institution expenditure fell 2.8% and 2.4% in volume; the results show that on the production side Gross Value Added at basic prices grew 12.4%, with Trade up 28.8%, Accommodation and Restaurants up 224.5% and administrative and support service activities up 58.4%, the primary sector down 6.4% and the secondary and tertiary sectors up 4.4% and 15.5%; net taxes on products rose 39.1%, contributing 5.1 percentage points to the total change in GDP.

a3992.speaker: Professor Ntobeko Ntusi, president and CEO of the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC)
a3992.speech: “South Africa is the biggest recipient of NIH funding outside of the US”, he told Spotlight ; “[T]he consequences will be catastrophic if [funding] is stopped… for science that is important for the whole world” ; said South Africa plays a critical role in advancing HIV science, adding that “many of the major trials that have advanced our understanding of both the effective strategies for HIV management, as well as understanding the mechanisms of disease emanated from South Africa”.

a3992.speaker: Professor Ntobeko Ntusi, president and CEO of the SAMRC (on the SAMRC's exposure to the cuts)
a3992.speech: Said that the SAMRC is currently “heavily exposed” to the halting of grants from USAID and the CDC, with research programmes supported by USAID and the CDC already being stopped ; “In addition to support for HIV research, we have significant CDC grant funding in our burden of disease research unit, the research unit that publishes weekly statistics on morbidity and mortality in South Africa” ; “Our health systems research unit has a number of CDC grants which have been stopped [and] in our gender and health research unit we had a portfolio of CDC funding which also has been stopped” ; said there will also be major staffing ramifications at the SAMRC as well as at universities, and that if funding from the NIH is stopped “there would be huge fallout, we just wouldn't be able to cover the hundreds of staff that are employed through the NIH granting process” ; said the SAMRC's combined annual income from US grants (NIH, CDC and USAID) is 28% of its total earnings for the 2025/2026 financial year: “So, this is substantial - effectively a third of our income is from US federal agencies.”

a3992.speaker: Professor Ntobeko Ntusi, president and CEO of the SAMRC (on impacts beyond health)
a3992.speech: Said the executive order halting aid to South Africa will be felt across a range of different development initiatives such as water and sanitation, and climate change.

a3992.speaker: The White House / US executive order of 7 February
a3992.speech: The order was issued to respond to what the White House called “egregious actions” by South Africa, specifically pointing to the Expropriation Act and the country's accusation of genocide against Israel at the International Court of Justice as the primary reasons for the funding freeze.

a3992.speaker: Impact Global Health (NPO that tracks health research spending)
a3992.speech: According to Impact Global Health, US spending accounts for just over half (55%) of all spending on global health research around the world, the US spent $5.4 billion on global health research in 2022, and the NIH contributed 65% of global financing for HIV research between 2007 and 2022.

a3992.speaker: Treatment Action Group (New York-based policy think tank)
a3992.speech: According to the Treatment Action Group, the NIH provided 34% of tuberculosis research financing in 2023.

a3992.speaker: Robert F Kennedy Jr, US health secretary nominee
a3992.speech: Has called for cutting the NIH's infectious disease research spending to focus more on chronic diseases.

a3992.speaker: Spotlight (health journalism publication)
a3992.speech: Spotlight understands that the limited waivers and exceptions to the cuts have so far been poorly communicated and that many HIV services remain in limbo.

a4006.speaker: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) (public notice)
a4006.speech: Issued a sharp public rebuke, accusing media outlets of “mischievous misrepresentation” and categorically denouncing as “inaccurate” widespread media reports claiming the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had “found no evidence of corruption” or had “cleared” Cecilia Dapaah, stating they are a dangerous distortion of the facts presented in its own Half-Yearly Report ; concluded with a stern warning to media houses, urging them to report with “precision and fidelity to the text of official documents” to ensure responsible communication on matters of significant national interest.

a4006.speaker: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) (public notice)
a4006.speech: Explained that its report found “no direct and immediate evidence of corruption”, which does not mean the person is innocent or that there was no evidence at all, but that while the case did not meet the strict standard for a direct corruption charge, there were still serious reasons to keep investigating.

a4006.speaker: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) (public notice)
a4006.speech: Detailed how its probe, which ran parallel to an FBI investigation it had initiated, uncovered “strong indications of suspected money laundering and structuring”, findings falling squarely within EOCO’s mandate, prompting the OSP to refer the case to that agency ; revealed that “the previous leadership of EOCO did not act on it and returned the docket” ; confirmed the docket has now been returned to EOCO’s new leadership upon their request.

a4009.speaker: Amos Makalla, Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) Secretary for Ideology, Publicity, and Training
a4009.speech: “CHADEMA is collecting funds under the pretext of mobilizing the public to reject the elections and halt the electoral process, but there is a hidden agenda. These people, especially senior leaders whose families are not in Tanzania, intend to use the funds raised by the tone-tone campaign to ‘purchase’ Ebola and Mpox viruses and bring them to Tanzania to spread, to ensure that the elections do not take place” ; “This is a secret plan they are coordinating, they have already met with some people, and the fundraising they are conducting is aimed at acquiring these viruses. Their intention is that as the election approaches, as months nears, people in Tanzania will fall sick with Ebola and Mpox. This is a dangerous matter. Those of you who are contributing to ‘tone-tone’ are funding the purchase of Ebola viruses so that they can be introduced into Tanzania.”

a4009.speaker: Amani Golugwa, CHADEMA Deputy Secretary General
a4009.speech: “Amos Makalla, you have spoken very recklessly, and you must take responsibility for your words, shame on you. Reflect on this and retract your words within seven days.”

a4009.speaker: John Heche, CHADEMA Vice-Chairperson
a4009.speech: “Amos Makalla is claiming that we are going to purchase viruses, yet he has not told Tanzanians which store sells these viruses and at what price so that we can inform the WHO to destroy them at their source. These are called biological attacks, he is an economic saboteur” ; “He is an ignorant person who thinks Tanzanians are stupid. The government newspaper Habari Leo has published this story. I ask you Mr. Chairman to instruct our lawyers to file a case against these individuals.”

a4009.speaker: Ado Shaibu, ACT Wazalendo General Secretary
a4009.speech: “To set the record straight, ACT Wazalendo will write to the Registrar of Political Parties, demanding action per the Political Parties Act regarding the false and fascist statement made by CCM’s Publicity Secretary, Amos Makalla, against CHADEMA” ; “This statement is not just an attack on CHADEMA but also an attack on democracy and the nation. It is a reckless remark that should not be tolerated.”

a4009.speaker: Fatma Karume, lawyer
a4009.speech: “There is a big problem in Tanzania. Questions for Makalla: Who is breeding the Ebola virus?, in which country is this person located, and at what price is it being sold, why hasn’t the government informed the WHO? Makalla is a scholar and a leader. To claim that CHADEMA is planning a biological attack against Tanzanians without evidence is not politics.”

a4009.speaker: Habari Leo (government daily, statement)
a4009.speech: Said in a statement released on Sunday, after retracting the story from its social media pages: “We have decided to remove it due to the lack of response from the other side, as well as concerns and opinions expressed by some of our viewers.”

a4009.speaker: U.S. Centre for Disease Control (CDC)
a4009.speech: Has listed smallpox and Ebola as category A of the bioterrorism agents: “High-priority agents include organisms that pose a risk to national security because they can be easily disseminated or transmitted from person to person; result in high mortality rates and have the potential for major public health impact; might cause public panic and social disruption; and require special action for public health preparedness.”

a4009.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a4009.speech: Has yet to issue a statement regarding the claim made by the ruling party spokesperson (non-response).

a4061.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) and other public health entities
a4061.speech: Have warned that the pandemic will be more lethal in Africa than in the developed regions thus far.

a4061.speaker: Heads of State and Government of the Horn of Africa countries
a4061.speech: At the end of March 2020 decided to adopt a joint strategy and to strengthen coordination and regional responses to curb the spread of the virus in the sub region; they announced their intention to coordinate regional response to the pandemic, and recognized the central role and the need for proactive support of the African Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) through building the capacity of healthcare providers and emergency response teams, as well as provision of medical supplies including testing kits.

a4166.speaker: Damian Maghambayi, councillor of Mukwe Constituency
a4166.speech: Urged the Minister of Finance to intervene in the upgrade of the Divundu Muhembo border road ; “And this is the road that links Namibia with Botswana, and it's also good for international exports. Where we are linking neighbouring countries, such as Botswana and South Africa, you name them in SADC. Therefore, the honourable minister will have the opportunity to see it for himself. This road has been designed to be upgraded to a bitumen standard, and every year we are told the project has been postponed to the next financial year. During this financial year, we really need you, honourable minister, to speak to the sector ministry to expedite the implementation of this project.”

a4166.speaker: Iipumbu Shiimi, Minister of Finance
a4166.speech: Acknowledged the challenges and need for upgrading the Divundu Muhembo border road ; “Obviously, as Namibia, we continue to invest heavily in our road infrastructure, and you know that we are the best on the continent. But we should continue to invest more in funding roads such as this one. This one is very significant for two reasons. First of all, it connects the two people of the two countries, Botswana and Namibia. In those countries, people are highly interconnected; they have families on both sides. Second, the road passes through the Bwabwata National Park, which is important for tourism. So the experience has been good, but I believe we should invest in upgrading our road infrastructure, and this one is not going to be an exception. We will continue to upgrade it until it has been upgraded to a level where we are all going to be satisfied.”

a4198.speaker: US State Department cable sent by Secretary of State Marco Rubio to all US diplomatic posts
a4198.speech: Calls for immediate “stop work” orders on existing foreign assistance and pauses new aid; provides a waiver only for emergency food assistance and foreign military financing for Israel and Egypt; said that in the coming month the administration will develop standards for a review of whether the assistance is “aligned with President Trump’s foreign policy agenda” ; “Decisions whether to continue, modify, or terminate programs will be made following this review,” noting such a review should be completed within 85 days.

a4198.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (public statement Wednesday)
a4198.speech: “every dollar we spend, every program we fund, and every policy we pursue must be justified with the answer to three simple questions: Does it make America safer? Does it make America stronger? Does it make America more prosperous?”

a4198.speaker: A humanitarian official (anonymous)
a4198.speech: “It’s a global freak out at the moment.”

a4198.speaker: InterAction, an alliance of international nongovernmental organizations (statement)
a4198.speech: Said the freeze “interrupts critical life-saving work including clean water to infants, basic education for kids, ending the trafficking of girls, and providing medications to children and others suffering from disease. It stops assistance in countries critical to U.S. interests, including Taiwan, Syria, and Pakistan.” ; “The recent stop-work cable from the State Department suspends programs that support America’s global leadership and creates dangerous vacuums that China and our adversaries will quickly fill.”

a4198.speaker: One humanitarian official (anonymous)
a4198.speech: Said the pause is incredibly disruptive and said the specifics of the cable are “as bad as can be.”

a4198.speaker: Another official (anonymous)
a4198.speech: Told CNN that while they expected there to be cuts or changes to assistance to specific areas, they were not expecting such a sweeping and immediate pause; said that the humanitarian needs worldwide are acute and a freeze in assistance from the US could be detrimental.

a4198.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a4198.speech: Claimed that the US “foreign aid industry and bureaucracy are not aligned with American interests and in many cases antithetical to American values.”

a4198.speaker: One of the officials (anonymous)
a4198.speech: Noted that assistance programs, such as those related to global health, which are targeted by the freeze, are in the US’ interest and had enjoyed bipartisan support: “Making sure there are not pandemics is in our interest. Global stability is in our interest.”

a4198.speaker: Democratic Reps. Gregory Meeks of New York and Lois Frankel of Florida (letter to Rubio)
a4198.speech: Said that programs that appear affected by the freeze such as the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and the President’s Malaria Initiative (PMI) “depend on an uninterrupted supply of medicines”; added that people around the world — such as in conflict-ridden Gaza, Sudan, Haiti and Ukraine — rely on the continued flow of aid from the United States ; “Congress has appropriated and cleared these funds for use, and it is our constitutional duty to make sure these funds are spent as directed. These funds respond directly to your stated challenge of carrying out a foreign policy that makes the United States stronger, safer, and more prosperous.”

a4198.speaker: The International AIDS Society
a4198.speech: Warned on Saturday that halting PEPFAR would place millions of lives in jeopardy.

a4198.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, IAS President (statement)
a4198.speech: “This is a matter of life or death. PEPFAR provides lifesaving antiretrovirals for more than 20 million people — and stopping its funding essentially stops their HIV treatment. If that happens, people are going to die and HIV will resurge.”

a4223.speaker: Prof Makala Lilemba, academician, author and scholar (opinion article)
a4223.speech: Writes that during the colonial period Namibians’ lives were dehumanised by the German and South African colonial masters, and that in this era “kleptocracy, which means rule by thieves, was hatched and nursed throughout the colonial period” ; argues that kleptocracy “is not just a later development, but it is embedded from the outset and well-advocated and planned,” with key features including elite capture at birth, where founding leaders consolidate wealth through state assets, land grabs or foreign aid siphoning, institutionalised corruption with no separation of powers, and anti-corruption agencies that exist only symbolically and victimise the so-called ‘small fish’ ; states that in many African countries foreign powers and corporations extract resources with the blessing of corrupt leaders and that money paid by foreign exploitative nations, aid and loans, funds private luxuries, not public services ; says Namibia “was looted and her resources taken and stashed in foreign lands and banks,” and that although one would have thought kleptocracy would be nipped in the bud after Independence in 1990, “the political campaigns and manifestos were simply smokescreens for corruption” and the kleptocratic system “in some quarters in this country has continued unabated,” witnessed by millions of dollars disappearing without a trace.

a4223.speaker: Moleah (1983), cited source
a4223.speech: Colonisers felt that democracy and rational thinking were not suited for Namibians (Moleah, 1983).

a4223.speaker: Ajamu (1997), cited source
a4223.speech: Calls this process of colonising African knowledge ‘intellectual colonialism.’

a4223.speaker: Hotep (2003), cited source
a4223.speech: States that this imposition has been more pronounced among the Christianised, Western-trained African intellectuals.

a4223.speaker: Walter Rodney (1973), ‘How Europe Underdeveloped Africa’
a4223.speech: Explicitly explains how the colonial powers looted the resources of Africa to build their empires.

a4223.speaker: Mazrui (1986), cited source
a4223.speech: Questions the civility of Europeans who first came to Africa to civilise and educate Africans, ending in underdeveloping the continent; emphasises that it was Europeans who were supposed to be civilised and educated instead of the Africans, because of the heinous crimes they committed against Africans in their own countries.

a4346.speaker: Presidency of Ghana (press statement, September 1, 2025)
a4346.speech: Said the move was in accordance with Article 149 (9) of the 1992 Constitution ; "President John Dramani Mahama has, in accordance with Article 146(9) of the 1992 Constitution, removed the Chief Justice, Her Ladyship Justice Gertrude Araba Esaaba Sackey Torkonoo, from office with immediate effect. This follows receipt of the report of the Committee constituted under Article 146(6) to inquire into a petition submitted by a Ghanaian citizen, Mr Daniel Ofori. After considering the petition and the evidence, the Committee found that the grounds of stated misbehaviour under Article 146(1) had been established and recommended her removal from office. Under Article 146(9), the President is required to act in accordance with the committee's recommendation."

a4346.speaker: Committee of inquiry chaired by Justice Gabriel Pwamang (report)
a4346.speech: Presented its report on Monday morning and found that the grounds of stated misbehaviour under Article 146(1) had been established and recommended her removal from office.

a4346.speaker: 1992 Constitution of Ghana, Article 146(9)
a4346.speech: Stipulates that "The President shall, in each case, act in accordance with the recommendations of the committee".

a4346.speaker: Daniel Ofori, Ghanaian citizen (petition)
a4346.speech: Had petitioned the President to remove Justice Torkornoo on grounds of stated misbehaviour as Chief Justice.

a4346.speaker: Presidency of Ghana (April 2025 announcement)
a4346.speech: Announced that President Mahama had received petitions asking that Justice Torkornoo be removed from office.

a4596.speaker: The Namibian, Republikein and Namibian Sun (newspaper articles)
a4596.speech: A series of articles castigated the draft Namibia Investment Promotion and Facilitation Bill for the perceived 'Super minister' powers it accords.

a4596.speaker: Dr Michael Humavindu, Deputy Executive Director, Namibian Ministry of Industrialisation and Trade (opinion article author)
a4596.speech: Argued that the draft NIPA is actually a modern piece of legislation that errs on the side of caution and gradualism as opposed to straightjacket provisions, and that "nowhere in the Bill is the minister empowered to approve all economic sector and business activities as wrongly alluded to by the media"; said the media articles took the minister's determination powers over Reserved Economic Sectors and Business Activities and wrongly abrogated it across all investments, showing deficiencies in the nation's economic journalism competencies, and urged that the country "reset and ensure the passing of the bill as soon as we all attune ourselves to the true orientation, intentions, and content of the Bill."

a4615.speaker: SADC leaders
a4615.speech: Have called for greater regional cooperation to address conflict, terrorism and other emerging security threats facing Southern Africa.

a4615.speaker: Dinah Marathe, Botswana's Police Services Commissioner
a4615.speech: Has called on SADC member states to double their efforts in the fight against drug trafficking, as Cannabis (dagga) smuggling is reaching alarming levels.

a4615.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, Tanzanian President
a4615.speech: Said East African nations must 'stand firm' against cross-border youth protests, describing Gen Z-led movements as attempts to 'spread chaos' and destabilise the region.

a4615.speaker: Chairperson of the Southern African Regional Police Chiefs Cooperation Organisation (SARPCCO)
a4615.speech: Has called for political support from governments across the region to strengthen the fight against transnational organised crime.

a4615.speaker: Joseph Shikongo, Police Inspector General (Namibia)
a4615.speech: Has said policies and resolutions adopted by the Southern African Regional Police Chiefs Cooperation Organisation (SARPCCO) are producing results, despite persistent political, economic and social challenges facing member states.

a4615.speaker: Majority of member states of the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC)
a4615.speech: Have expressed concern over the recent military deployment by the United States in the Caribbean, particularly near Venezuelan waters.

a4696.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a4696.speech: Has commended countries and organisations that responded to the government’s appeal for humanitarian assistance as the country grapples with an El Nino-induced drought.

a4696.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a4696.speech: In his State of the Nation Address (SONA) to the second session of the 10th Parliament, said the El Nino-induced drought constrained the country’s growth across all economic sectors, particularly agriculture ; “However, under the Food Deficit Mitigation Program, communities requiring food assistance in rural areas are receiving grain, while vulnerable households in urban areas are benefitting through the Cash-for-Cereals Program.” ; “Of particular note is the school feeding component which has been designed to avail at least one decent meal per day for all learners in communities hard hit by the drought. Be assured that no Zimbabwean will go without food.”

a4696.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a4696.speech: Said the Grain Marketing Board has established agro-shops, mainly in rural depots, as part of measures to ensure food availability at more affordable prices, complemented by the establishment of 35 000 Village Business Units supported by the Presidential Borehole Drilling Program, to enhance food and nutrition security at the household level.

a4696.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a4696.speech: “May I recognise and applaud the vital role played by our farmers in feeding our people and contributing to Zimbabwe’s agricultural self-reliance.” ; “A new record wheat harvest of 600 000 tons is projected from the 2024 winter crop. This is a result of our unity of purpose and effective policy frameworks,” while expressing optimism that the 2024–2025 summer cropping season will come good amid projections of normal to above normal rainfall in most provinces ; expressed satisfaction with the pace of inputs distribution under the Pfumvudza/Intwasa Presidential Climate-Proofed Agriculture Production Scheme ; “I congratulate ARDA (Agricultural and Rural Development Authority) for scooping the prestigious 2024 Africa Food Prize, in recognition of our people-centred transformative agriculture policies. For the upcoming summer season, ARDA has been given a target of 500 000 tons of cereals for the Strategic Grain Reserve.”

a4696.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a4696.speech: Said water harvesting remains critical to climate change mitigation and adaptation towards complementing rain-fed production systems ; stated that as a result, the full utilisation of small dams and weirs and the conveyancing around the bigger dams in the country is the top government priority.

a4800.speaker: Ivan Manhiça, Permanent Secretary at the Mozambican Health Ministry
a4800.speech: Said the Task Force will first have the mission of meeting health workers and partners to discuss the impact of reduced funding, “a fact that occurs amid an increasing frequency and severity of health emergencies in the country.” ; “With the creation of this task force, the Health Ministry is also aimed at identifying and implementing urgent reforms that ensure the continuity of quality services for Mozambicans” ; “This task force serves as a window in the search for solutions to mitigate the impact and allow ongoing projects to continue” ; Said the Task Force is expected to bring results in the short, medium, and long term, “allowing the health sector to have domestic financing alternatives, especially for key issues. The financing model must be balanced to ensure the sector functions better and reduce external dependence.”

a4815.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (New Year message)
a4815.speech: “As we enter 2025, I wish everyone a happy and prosperous New Year... Though 2024 posed numerous challenges to our citizens and households, I am confident that the New Year will bring brighter days. Economic indicators point to a positive and encouraging outlook for our nation. Fuel prices have gradually decreased, and we recorded foreign trade surpluses in three consecutive quarters. Foreign reserves have risen, and the Naira has strengthened against the US dollar, bringing greater stability. The stock market’s record growth has generated trillions of naira in wealth, and the surge in foreign investment reflects renewed confidence in our economy. Nevertheless, the cost of food and essential drugs remained a significant concern for many Nigerian households in 2024.”

a4815.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (New Year message)
a4815.speech: “In 2025, our government is committed to intensifying efforts to lower these costs by boosting food production and promoting local manufacturing of essential drugs and other medical supplies. We are resolute in our ambition to reduce inflation from its current high of 34.6% to 15%. With diligent work and God’s help, we will achieve this goal and provide relief to all our people.”

a4815.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (New Year message)
a4815.speech: “In this new year, my administration will further consolidate and increase access to credit for individuals and critical sectors of the economy to boost national economic output. To achieve this, the federal government will establish the National Credit Guarantee Company to expand risk-sharing instruments for financial institutions and enterprises. The Company—expected to start operations before the end of the second quarter—is a partnership of government institutions, such as the Bank of Industry, Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, the Nigerian Sovereign Investment Agency, and Ministry of Finance Incorporated, the private sector, and multilateral institutions. This initiative will strengthen the confidence of the financial system, expand credit access, and support under-served groups such as women and youth.”

a4815.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (New Year message)
a4815.speech: “On a personal note, thank you for placing your confidence in me as your president. Your trust humbles me, and I promise to continue serving you diligently and wholeheartedly. We will continue to embark on necessary reforms to foster sustainable growth and prosperity for our nation. I seek your cooperation and collaboration at all times as we pursue our goal of a one trillion-dollar economy. Let us stay focused and united. We are on the right path to building a great Nigeria that will work for everyone. Let us not get distracted by a tiny segment of our population that still sees things through the prisms of politics, ethnicity, region, and religion.”

a4815.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (New Year message)
a4815.speech: “To achieve our national goals and objectives, we must become better citizens and uncompromising in our devotion and allegiance to Nigeria. Citizens’ moral rectitude and faith in our country are fundamental to the success of the Renewed Hope Agenda. In 2025, we will commit to promoting adherence to ethical principles, shared values, and beliefs under the National Identity Project. I will unveil the National Values Charter, already approved by the Federal Executive Council, in the first quarter of 2025. I will launch an ambitious national orientation campaign that fosters patriotism and love for our country and inspires citizens to rally together.”

a4815.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (New Year message)
a4815.speech: “The Youth Confab will begin in the first quarter of 2025, a testament to our commitment to youth inclusiveness and investment as nation-builders. The Ministry of Youth will soon announce the modalities for selecting the conference’s representatives from our diverse, youthful population.”

a4815.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (New Year message)
a4815.speech: “Let me use this New Year’s message to urge our governors and local council chairpersons to work closely with the central government to seize emerging opportunities in agriculture, livestock, and tax reforms and move our nation forward. I commend governors who have embraced our Compressed Natural Gas initiative by launching CNG-propelled public transport. I also congratulate those who have adopted electric vehicles as part of our national energy mix and transition. The Federal Government will always offer necessary assistance to the states. To all citizens, your sacrifices have not been in vain over the past 19 months.”

a4854.speaker: United States government, through the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a4854.speech: Announced an additional $10 million in humanitarian assistance to support regional operations to control locusts in Ethiopia, Kenya, and Somalia, bringing the U.S. government's regional humanitarian response to the locust outbreak to $19 million; the new funding will support locust detection, surveillance, and control operations across the region, including ground-based and aerial efforts.

a4939.speaker: Jeanne Josette Acacha Akoha, Director of Environmental and Social Assessments, Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) Benin
a4939.speech: told the press: "Preserving the environment is an obligation for the MCA-Benin programme, which must comply with Beninese regulations in this area but also comply with the agreement that the Beninese State signed with the United States, which stipulates that MCC funding cannot be used to undertake, finance or support activities that tend to harm the environment, health or safety." ; according to her, her unit ensures that the projects carried out under the programme take into account the necessary prevention or mitigation measures to avoid or minimise negative impacts and to amplify positive impacts so that the environmental and social balance is not affected.

a4939.speaker: Jeanne Josette Acacha Akoha, Director of Environmental and Social Assessments, Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) Benin
a4939.speech: said the environmental and social impact studies are completed and validated by the Certificate of Environmental Compliance, adding: "The environmental and social impact study is a process that makes it possible to ensure that environment-related factors are included in decision-making concerning the project."

a4939.speaker: Millennium Challenge Account (MCA-Benin) announcement
a4939.speech: has just announced several works within the port area, including the 300-metre extension of the sand-trapping groyne to block littoral drift and combat the silting up of the entrance channel and the port basin, the construction of two new berths with a total length of 600 metres and a depth of 15 metres for container ships, and the development of the aprons for unloading and storing containers.

a4939.speaker: Environmental and social impact studies (MCA-Benin, Port of Cotonou)
a4939.speech: made it possible to draw up an environmental assessment of the Port of Cotonou in its current operating phase, to analyse the major environmental risks and cumulative effects, to determine the potential environmental and social impacts of the project, to draw up an HIV/AIDS awareness plan, to cost mitigation measures, and to produce an environmental and social management plan and a framework for the environmental management system.

a5100.speaker: Israel
a5100.speech: Declared as its goal the elimination of Hamas.

a5159.speaker: Przemyslaw Bobak, EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation in Chad
a5159.speech: In his remarks, praised “the excellence of political and diplomatic relations” between the two partners and reaffirmed the EU’s tangible commitment through humanitarian assistance valued at €134 million for 2025.

a5159.speaker: Dr. Abdoulaye Sabre Fadoul, Minister of State, Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Chadians Abroad
a5159.speech: Acknowledged the uncertain international environment while highlighting the consistency of Chad’s partnership with the European Union; commended the EU’s adherence to “solidarity among peoples, multilateralism, and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States.”

a5173.speaker: Minister in charge of petroleum of Niger
a5173.speech: Announced during the council of ministers on 24 June that, on the instructions of the Head of State, a working group had been set up, tasked with considering a revision of the structure of fuel prices with a view to lowering the price at the pump.

a5173.speaker: Mahaman Nouri, President of the Association for the Defence of Consumers' Rights (ADDC-Wadata)
a5173.speech: Explained in an interview granted to ANP that the establishment of the committee responsible for revising the structure of fuel prices creates hope among Nigeriens. “A reduction will be very well received by Nigerien consumers, because we know that with current prices, transport costs have risen sharply - over short distances one has to pay more than 500 FCFA, and in certain areas 1,000 FCFA and more.” ; said there must be reflection on the impact that this revision, if downward, would have on several activities, notably on transport, on freight prices and on the reduction of prices of goods on the market: “This revision, if it is downward, will make it possible to have an impact on all the chains of fuel use and particularly on the price of consumer goods.”

a5173.speaker: Ibrahim Bana, influencer and civil society actor
a5173.speech: Said the revision of fuel prices has been a strong social demand since the beginning of oil production in Niger, “even if it did not have the approval of the authorities for some ten years” ; announced that by setting up this committee, “the president of the CNSP creates the conditions for the realisation of this old dream of Nigeriens, that of having access to petrol and diesel at a price within the reach of all Nigeriens.”

a5342.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a5342.speech: Sounded the alarm on Friday over escalating hunger in west and central Africa as needs reach "record levels", saying more than 36 million people are struggling to meet their food needs, a number that could rise to 52 million people during the lean season between harvests this summer ; "Persistent conflict, displacement, economic deterioration and recurrent extreme weather in west and central Africa are driving millions of people towards emergency levels of hunger." ; had previously referred to an "unprecedented crisis" at the end of March due to a 40% reduction in its funding for 2025; said at the end of April that it would have to reduce its workforce by 25% to 30% worldwide; said five million people risk losing assistance altogether unless urgent funding is received.

a5342.speaker: Margot van der Velden, WFP regional director for west and central Africa
a5342.speech: "We are at a tipping point, and millions of lives are at stake." ; "Without immediate funding, WFP will be forced to scale down even further both in the number of people reached and the size of food rations distributed."

a5426.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a5426.speech: Said cattle marketing during the third quarter increased by a marginal 1.5%, with 99 451 cattle marketed compared to 98 016 heads marketed during the corresponding quarter of 2023 ; said the growth recorded is attributed to improved throughput at export-approved abattoirs, which increased by 23.3% ; added that export-approved abattoirs north of the veterinary cordon fence performed relatively well during the third quarter, with the Rundu abattoir slaughtering 1 017 animals while Katima Mulilo abattoir slaughtered 957 ; “Regrettably, the demand for local weaners by South African feedlots and farmers declined during the quarter.” ; said this led to a subsequent decline in the number of animals exported on hoof, recording a total of 47 714 heads exported - which is 7.7% lower than the 51 690 heads exported during the third quarter of 2023.

a5426.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a5426.speech: Said that year-on-year, livestock prices within the cattle sector faced downward pressure and recorded lower levels during the quarter ; said beef exports totaled 6.6 million kilograms during the first two months of the third quarter, growing by 60.8% and bringing year-to-date total beef exports to 17.3 million kilograms, 66.2% higher than the 2023 level ; said year-to-date beef imports, primarily in the form of processed and offal products, are down by 0.6%, pointing to a marginal reduction in availability of locally produced offal.

a5426.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a5426.speech: According to the LLPB, the sheep sector recorded a drop in overall marketing activities by 6.7% as a result of a decline across all marketing segments during the third quarter: "Live exports of sheep for the first time this year fell by 4.1%, with only 144 045 animals exported during 2024 compared to 150 175 animals exported during the corresponding quarter of 2023."

a5426.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a5426.speech: Noted of the goat sector, which declined by 2.9%, that “The contraction is owed to a fall in live exports and slaughtering at local abattoirs.”

a5454.speaker: Cédric Nkurunziza, young entrepreneur, founder of the company “Terimbere Burundi Technology” in Gitega commune
a5454.speech: In an interview granted to the newspaper Le Renouveau from Gitega, indicates that the security of property and persons is an unavoidable factor in promoting the country's development, and that it also attracts foreign investors, from which the country benefits; it was in this framework that he saw fit to join with other young people to create a company, a cooperative spirit that allowed them to raise start-up capital of fifty thousand Burundian francs, after which they decided to enrich their talent through research carried out on the internet ; says the automatic lamps they now make have the advantage of being triggered by a motion detector and can thus detect animal or human presence and then raise the alarm if needed; according to him it is a lighting system that saves energy since the lamp switches on at night and goes off during the day, so the user has no worry about forgetting to switch it off, which allows him to be rational in managing the related funds and to direct that saving into other income-generating activities; the system also guarantees the security of property and persons in so far as its user can simulate his presence ; stresses that the company gives priority to the manufacturing quality of its products, which has allowed it to reach a current capital of nine million Burundian francs.

a5454.speaker: Cédric Nkurunziza, young entrepreneur, founder of the company “Terimbere Burundi Technology” in Gitega commune
a5454.speech: Suggests that the project initiated by this company deserves to be extended throughout the country in order to strengthen the security of property and persons, which would positively influence the country's socio-economic development; indicates that the company spares no effort to increase its production, since it can currently manufacture some twenty automatic lamps per week, and that it also intends to implement other strategies for increasing its production.

a5454.speaker: Cédric Nkurunziza, young entrepreneur, founder of the company “Terimbere Burundi Technology” in Gitega commune
a5454.speech: Deplores that some Burundians favour imports over locally manufactured goods, which holds back local development, and therefore calls on Burundians to love locally made products in order to support Burundian businesses.

a5483.speaker: Governments worldwide, including Ethiopia
a5483.speech: Have promised to end hunger, poverty and disease; they pledged to stop climate change, corruption and war while ensuring quality education and every other imaginable good.

a5483.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a5483.speech: Is now implausibly calling for a half trillion dollar annual SDG stimulus package.

a5483.speaker: Copenhagen Consensus Centre / economists working with the Copenhagen Consensus
a5483.speech: Economists working with the Copenhagen Consensus have identified 12 effective policies that would deliver enormous benefits across the SDGs at relatively low costs - for a total of 35 billion dollars annually - saving 4.2 million lives yearly and making the poorer world 1.1 trillion dollars more prosperous, with every dollar spent delivering 52 dollars of social benefits.

a6090.speaker: Georgetown Global Health (NGO)
a6090.speech: has called on governments at all levels to involve Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) in policy making processes at all levels, from program design to implementation and evaluation, saying this would ensure that the programs are responsive to the needs and priorities of the PWD community.

a6090.speaker: MaryAnn Emmanuel, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) Officer of Georgetown Global Health USAID Nigeria
a6090.speech: stated this during a training for stakeholders in Bauchi State ; She said PWDs face heightened risk of violence, exploitation and abuse both within their families and communities.

a6090.speaker: Network of Women with Disabilities in Nigeria, 2020 report
a6090.speech: according to a 2020 report by the Network of Women with Disabilities in Nigeria, 68% of women with disabilities have experienced some form of Gender-Based Violence, including physical, sexual, economical and emotional abuse.

a6205.speaker: Dr Mary Rose Giattas, Director of the MCGL project (JHPIEGO)
a6205.speech: Highlighted the successful partnership between JHPIEGO and the Tanzanian government: “We have had a very positive experience working closely with the Tanzanian government through the Ministry of Health. This collaboration has been instrumental in delivering health services since the launch of the first phase of our project in 2021.” ; Further explained that the initial phase focused on improving health institutions across 22 regions, boosting childhood vaccination for children under five years old and implementing the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination for girls to prevent cervical cancer.

a6205.speaker: Dr Mary Rose Giattas, Director of the MCGL project (JHPIEGO)
a6205.speech: “We are grateful for the progress we have made in supporting many Tanzanians through this project. Recognising the critical need in some regions, we decided to provide these vehicles as a key resource to improve the speed and efficiency of health service delivery.” ; Said the vehicles, valued between 110m/- and 129m/-, will significantly contribute to overcoming various healthcare challenges, including the timely provision of immunisation services.

a6205.speaker: Dr Grace Magembe, Deputy Permanent Health Secretary
a6205.speech: Expressed her gratitude and praised the collaboration between JHPIEGO and the government, reassuring the public that the vehicles would be utilised effectively: “On behalf of the President’s Office Regional Administration and Local Government and the local government authorities in the regions benefiting from the MCGL project, we extend our thanks for this generous donation. We assure you that the vehicles will be put to good use in advancing health services.”

a6205.speaker: Dr Samweli Lazier, Kagera Regional Medical Officer
a6205.speech: Emphasised the commitment to ensuring the new vehicles are used effectively: “We are grateful for the donation of this vehicle. As the Kagera Region, we will ensure it is used for specialised health services, helping the community access essential healthcare promptly.”

a6313.speaker: US study (on people taking immunosuppressive drugs after organ transplant)
a6313.speech: Has found that people taking drugs that suppress their immune systems (after having had an organ transplant, to stop the organ being rejected) appear to be hampered in their ability to generate antibodies after being vaccinated ; the study found that over half of the immunocompromised people it looked at had generated no antibodies even after receiving two vaccine doses.

a6313.speaker: Research on immunosuppressed kidney transplant patients
a6313.speech: Found that immunosuppressed kidney transplant patients did respond somewhat to being given a dose of a Covid-19 vaccine, but that they had weaker antibody responses than those with fully functioning immune systems.

a6313.speaker: UK preprint (early research awaiting peer review) on Pfizer/BioNTech and Oxford/AstraZeneca vaccines in at-risk groups
a6313.speech: Aimed to provide more information on how well the Pfizer/BioNTech and Oxford/AstraZeneca Covid-19 vaccines work in different at-risk groups, including patients with diabetes, chronic heart disease, chronic kidney disease, chronic liver disease, neurological conditions as well as those who are immunocompromised. Most groups generated strong antibody responses and were protected against symptomatic Covid-19 after being vaccinated. But in the immunocompromised, antibody levels were lower after two doses, and after their first dose they were less well protected against symptomatic Covid-19 than the other groups. However, after having had both doses, the immunocompromised group appeared to be well protected against the disease, even though their antibody levels were lower.

a6317.speaker: Russian Defense Ministry (Moscow)
a6317.speech: Has said the Ukrainian military has targeted two energy facilities in Russia's Belgorod Region over the past 24 hours ; "In violation of the Russia-US agreement, Kiev continues its unilateral attacks on Russian energy infrastructure," the ministry said in a statement on Sunday ; the statement read that on Saturday evening, more than 600 households were left without electricity in Belgorod Region's Shebekinsky District as a result of the "deliberate shelling" of a local energy facility by Ukrainian forces, and added that on Sunday morning another bombardment of energy infrastructure by Kiev's troops led to power shortages in the village of Stepnoye in Krasnoyaruzhsky District.

a6317.speaker: Vladimir Zelensky, Ukrainian leader
a6317.speech: Also said that his country would abide by the truce.

a6317.speaker: Russian military
a6317.speech: Has since accused Kiev's forces of breaching the partial ceasefire on an almost daily basis.

a6317.speaker: The Kremlin
a6317.speech: Said that Russia is abiding by the truce and has refrained from targeting Ukrainian energy facilities in order to build goodwill with Washington, but it also warned that Moscow reserves the right to pull out of the 30-day agreement early if it is not honored by Kiev.

a6317.speaker: Maria Zakharova, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman
a6317.speech: Has previously suggested that Ukraine is deliberately violating the partial ceasefire in an attempt to undermine peace initiatives and the dialogue between Russia and the US.

a6482.speaker: World Health Organization
a6482.speech: Is now recommending that countries include the newly approved HIV prevention drug lenacapavir as a tool in their efforts to fight HIV infections, especially for groups most at risk and in areas where the burden of HIV remains high; its landmark guidance, released at the 13th International AIDS Society Conference in Kigali on July 14, endorses the drug’s use every six months.

a6482.speaker: Dr. Meg Doherty, director of WHO’s Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis and Sexually Transmitted Infections Programmes
a6482.speech: “These new recommendations are designed for real-world use. WHO is working closely with countries and partners to support the implementation.” ; “The first recommendation is that a long-acting injectable, lenacapavir, should be offered as an additional prevention choice for people at risk for HIV and as part of combination prevention. With that, we call it a strong recommendation with moderate to high certainty of the evidence.”

a6482.speaker: WHO guidelines (second recommendation)
a6482.speech: That rapid diagnostic tests, like at-home tests, can be used to screen someone for HIV when they are starting, continuing, or stopping long-acting medication to prevent infection, called pre-exposure prophylaxis, or PrEP; WHO also streamlined HIV testing protocols to support injectable PrEP uptake in community settings, pharmacies, and telehealth contexts.

a6482.speaker: Health leaders, including WHO’s Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a6482.speech: Touted lenacapavir as “the next best thing” to an HIV vaccine.

a6482.speaker: Purpose trial data
a6482.speech: In one study, zero infections occurred among participants receiving lenacapavir, compared to significant infection rates in the pill-based PrEP group.

a6570.speaker: Alpha S. Diallo, Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
a6570.speech: Delivered a speech at the opening of the workshop and remarked that "the American people stand alongside the Djiboutian people to support all initiatives that make it possible for inequalities linked to gender and social inclusion to be better taken into account by all actors of economic and social life," before expressing his hope that the workshop would open up prospects for cooperation and collaboration among the various actors taking part in it.

a6627.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6627.speech: Reechoed President Joseph Nyumah Boakai’s appreciation to the CEO and the Senior Management of the MCC and the American Government for the country’s selection. He recalled the transformative impact the first MCC grant has had on Liberia through the restoration of the Mont Coffee Hydro dam, the setting up of the Liberia Electricity Regulatory Commission, and support to the LWSC for restoring water pipes to Monrovia, among others.

a6627.speaker: Kyeh Kim, MCC Vice President for Compact Operations
a6627.speech: Expressed her enthusiasm for continuing the partnership, saying, “We’re excited to continue working with Liberia.” ; was happy to reveal that there was strong enthusiasm for Liberia among MCC Board members at their last board meeting, where the country was selected for the second compact ; informed that Mr. Small will visit Liberia to be followed by Vice President Kim to engage with the Minister of Finance and other senior government officials and stakeholders on the Liberia Compact.

a6724.speaker: His Holiness, Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad (aba), Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community
a6724.speech: Said that he would continue mentioning details of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah.

a6724.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (ra), author of The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (quoted by His Holiness)
a6724.speech: Writes that it is common for flaws to be left undetected in agreements which later become the result of significant outcomes, and that in the Treaty of Hudaibiyah a deficiency went undetected, as although the return of Muslim men was clearly stipulated, there was no mention of women from the people of Makkah who would accept Islam and join the Muslims; recounts that Ummi Kulthum, daughter of the idolater chieftain ‘Uqbah bin Abi Mu‘it and maternal sister of Hazrat ‘Uthman bin ‘Affan, reached Madinah on foot and accepted Islam, and that the Holy Prophet (sa) gave a verdict in her favour and sent her relatives back.

a6724.speaker: Relatives of Ummi Kulthum / the Quraish claimants
a6724.speech: Claimed that although the word ‘man’ had been used in the treaty, in actuality the agreement was general and affected both men and women equally, and demanded her return.

a6724.speaker: Ummi Kulthum
a6724.speech: Contended for an exception in the case of women because a woman belongs to a weaker gender and holds a subordinate position to men, so that to return her would be equivalent to tossing her into the mouth of spiritual death and thus depriving her of Islam.

a6724.speaker: The Qur’an (revealed verse cited in the sermon)
a6724.speech: “When believing women come to you as refugees, examine them, and if they prove to be virtuous and sincere, send them not back to the disbelievers but if they are married women, return to their disbelieving husbands their dowries.”

a6724.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (ra), author of The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (quoted by His Holiness)
a6724.speech: Writes that among the conditions of the agreement of Hudaibiyah was that if an individual from among the Quraish became Muslim and came to Madinah the people of Madinah should return him, while if a Muslim denounced Islam and headed to Makkah the people of Makkah would not return him; that this condition at first seemed a means of disgrace for the Muslims, so much so that even Hazrat ‘Umar (ra) was very displeased and restless, but soon proved to be a means of weakness for the Quraish and strength for the Muslims; and recounts the account of Abu Basir ‘Utbah bin Usaid Thaqafi, the settlement at Siful-Bahr, and the Quraish’s eventual request to have the Muhajirin recalled to Madinah.

a6724.speaker: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (sa)
a6724.speech: Had stated in the beginning that if a Muslim became apostate and left Madinah then he was a rotten limb whose amputation was actually better, whereas if an individual became Muslim pure-heartedly and left Makkah he would become a means to strengthen Islam irrespective of where he resided, and ultimately Allah would clear a way for his deliverance.

a6724.speaker: Abu Basir ‘Utbah bin Usaid Thaqafi
a6724.speech: Lamented, “I am a Muslim, these people shall give me grief in Makkah and shall coerce me to denounce Islam.”

a6724.speaker: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (sa)
a6724.speech: “We are bound by the agreement and cannot keep you here. If you are patient for the sake of God, He will open a way for you. We are constrained by the treaty and cannot act in offense to the agreement.”

a6724.speaker: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (sa)
a6724.speech: On seeing the fleeing man’s fearful state said, “It seems as if he has been afflicted by some fear or terror.”

a6724.speaker: The fleeing member of the Quraish party
a6724.speech: Panting for breath and trembling, said to the Holy Prophet (sa), “My companion has been killed and I am also as if in the mouth of death.”

a6724.speaker: Abu Basir ‘Utbah bin Usaid Thaqafi
a6724.speech: Said to the Holy Prophet (sa), “O Messenger of Allah! You handed me over to the Quraish and now your duty has been fulfilled. However, God has granted me deliverance from a cruel people and now you have no responsibility over me.”

a6724.speaker: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (sa)
a6724.speech: Spontaneously said: “Woe to his mother, this man is kindling the fire of war. If only there was someone to control him.”

a6724.speaker: Sahih Bukhari (hadith collection cited)
a6724.speech: “[When he heard that he knew that he would be returned to them]”

a6724.speaker: The Quraish of Makkah (delegation to the Holy Prophet)
a6724.speech: Pleaded, on account of their relation to him, that he call the Muhajirin of Siful-Bahr to Madinah and make them a part of his political system, and of their own accord forfeited the condition of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah stipulating that ‘New Muslims of Makkah shall not be granted protection in Madinah’.

a6724.speaker: His Holiness, Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad (aba), Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community
a6724.speech: Said that non-Muslim historians often misconstrue historical events and raise allegations as a result, and that they have done the same when it comes to the Treaty of Hudaibiyah.

a6724.speaker: Christian historians/writers (as characterised in the sermon)
a6724.speech: Have raised two objections with relation to the Treaty of Hudaibiyah: that the Holy Prophet’s (sa) exclusion of women from the conditions of the treaty was not permissible because the treaty’s words were general and included both men and women; and that in the account of Abu Basir the Holy Prophet (sa) broke the spirit of the agreement by indicating that Abu Basir could establish a separate party and run his affairs independently instead of returning to Makkah.

a6724.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (ra), author of The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (quoted by His Holiness)
a6724.speech: Responds that the agreement was with the Quraish of Makkah, who were at war with the Holy Prophet (sa) from the beginning and accustomed to objecting to even the smallest of things, yet did not object to this action or consider it against the agreement — so critics who came 1300 years later, to whom many finer details were hidden, have no right to raise such an allegation; and notes that the Qur’an, Ahadith and the history of Arabia are replete with allegations levelled by the infidels of Makkah, but contain not the slightest hint of an allegation that the Muslims acted against the Treaty of Hudaibiyah.

a6724.speaker: Heraclius, King of Rome (Caesar)
a6724.speech: Summoned Abu Sufyan to his royal court and asked him certain questions about the Holy Prophet (sa), among them: “Has this claimant to prophethood from your people ever broken an agreement?”

a6724.speaker: Abu Sufyan bin Harb, chieftain of Makkah
a6724.speech: “Nay, Muhammad (sa) has never proven treacherous in the matter of his covenants. However, in these days, we are at a truce with him, but I do not know how he shall deal until the conclusion of this agreement.” Abu Sufyan said that throughout the entire course of this dialogue, except for this phrase, he could say nothing more to produce a possible doubt in the heart of Heraclius against the Holy Prophet (sa).

a6862.speaker: Keir Starmer, British Prime Minister
a6862.speech: “We will continue to defend Israel’s right to defend itself, but it is important that we be a state committed to international law,” he replied when questioned by the leader of the opposition. “It is a difficult matter, I acknowledge that, but this is a legal decision, not a political one,” he added, arguing that the “legal framework is clear” and that, with the review of the arms export licences, a “clear legal conclusion” had been reached.

a6862.speaker: Keir Starmer, British Prime Minister
a6862.speech: Assured that the United Kingdom’s allies “understand” the decision, confirming that he had informed the United States and Israel beforehand.

a6862.speaker: Rishi Sunak, leader of the opposition and former British prime minister
a6862.speech: Questioned Starmer about the decision to suspend arms export licences to Israel.

a6862.speaker: Legal review of arms export licences (UK government analysis)
a6862.speech: The decision was based on the conclusions of a legal review which found that there was “a risk” that the weapons would be used in violation of international humanitarian law in the conflict between Israel and Hamas in the Gaza Strip.

a6862.speaker: Israeli government, the British Jewish community and the Conservative opposition
a6862.speech: Have criticised the announcement made two days ago of the suspension of around 30 arms export licences to Israel out of a total of 350.

a6862.speaker: Yoav Gallant, Israeli Defence Minister
a6862.speech: Declared himself “deeply disappointed” by the decision.

a6862.speaker: John Kirby, spokesman for the United States National Security Council
a6862.speech: Stated on Tuesday that “at this time, the United States has not determined that (Israel) has violated international humanitarian law.”

a6862.speaker: British Labour government
a6862.speech: Since taking office in early July has repeated the calls, as its Conservative predecessor did, for an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages and the acceleration of humanitarian aid to Gaza.

a6862.speaker: Israel (government)
a6862.speech: Accuses the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) of employing “more than 400 terrorists” in Gaza.

a6862.speaker: Local authorities in Gaza, controlled by Hamas
a6862.speech: According to them, the offensive in Gaza has caused more than 40,800 deaths to date, in addition to 680 deaths in the West Bank and East Jerusalem.

a6904.speaker: Judge Carl Nichols, US federal judge (restraining order of 9 February 2025)
a6904.speech: In a restraining order issued on 9 February 2025, imposed an immediate freeze on any administrative leave proceedings concerning the 2,200 employees under threat, and ordered the temporary reinstatement of 500 staff already suspended, guaranteeing they remain in post until 14 February at 11:59 p.m. (US time) ; The order also requires that the agency's employees retain unrestricted access to their communication, payment and security-alert systems until 14 February, and prohibits any evacuation of personnel out of their country of assignment before that date.

a6904.speaker: Judge Carl Nichols, US federal judge
a6904.speech: Highlighted the risks associated with a hasty disorganization of the agency; in his seven-page order he stresses that many of the staff concerned operate in high-risk environments where immediate access to security resources is paramount ; Emphasized that many USAID employees work in dangerous environments and that it is therefore essential that they have access to information about risks to their safety; he added that no legal remedy could repair the physical harm suffered by employees who had not been warned of imminent threats.

a6904.speaker: Two US workers' associations (unions)
a6904.speech: Filed this request on an emergency basis, denouncing an accelerated dismantling with potentially disastrous consequences.

a6904.speaker: Trump administration
a6904.speech: Justifies these cuts by budgetary and strategic imperatives.

a6908.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a6908.speech: Experts have expressed concern about a number of obstacles that could complicate the implementation of the strategy. Among them: the unstable security situation in the region, the lack of technical skills, as well as logistical problems due to closed export routes such as the border with Benin.

a7049.speaker: Mulambo Haimbe, Zambia’s Foreign Minister
a7049.speech: Warned diplomats against interfering in the country’s affairs, saying there was an “increasing tendency” by envoys to ignore diplomatic channels, and this could undermine the “spirit of mutual respect” ; Said that addressing the government through the media amounted to interference and was in breach of diplomatic conventions. “We remain open to addressing any matters of concern through appropriate diplomatic channels,” the minister added.

a7049.speaker: Michael Gonzales, US Ambassador to Zambia
a7049.speech: Called a press conference to announce that the US was cutting $50m (£37m) of health aid to Zambia because of the theft of life-saving medications that the US had provided for patients. He added that he had decided to go public after holding more than 30 fruitless meetings with senior Zambian officials ; Said that an inspection carried out by US officials at more than 2,000 pharmacies last year had found that most were selling drugs and medical supplies donated by the US.

a7049.speaker: Michael Gonzales, US Ambassador to Zambia
a7049.speech: Said the recent US measure was separate to the foreign aid freeze announced by President Donald Trump in January.

a7049.speaker: US embassy in Zambia
a7049.speech: Said it had presented its findings of the alleged corruption to Zambian officials in April last year, and had offered help to stop further theft and to bring the culprits to justice. However, no action was taken by the Zambian authorities, it added.

a7049.speaker: US embassy in Zambia (data)
a7049.speech: The US accounts for about a third of public health spending in Zambia, according to the US embassy.

a7049.speaker: Jacob Mwiimbu, Zambia’s Home Affairs Minister
a7049.speech: Said that a forensic audit on the alleged theft had been completed and handed over to security agencies for further action. About 75 people have been arrested in a countrywide crackdown that saw more than 400 health facilities raided over the alleged scam, he said. “There will be no sacred cows in this pursuit,” Mwiimbu added.

a7049.speaker: Elijah Muchima, Zambia’s Health Minister
a7049.speech: Earlier said the problem of theft predated the current government, which took office in 2021. Muchima also said several Zambian officials had been sacked following the thefts identified by the US, and that “an advanced digital stock tracking system” had been set up to monitor the supply of medicines ; Reassured Zambians that there were sufficient stocks of all drugs so there was “no immediate risk of shortages”.

a7049.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, Zambia’s President
a7049.speech: In March said Trump had “slapped us on both cheeks”, saying it was time for his country to strengthen its treasury to procure its own medicines.

a7282.speaker: Chief Adebayo Adelabu, Minister of Power
a7282.speech: Lauded the development partners' developmental role in the power sector over time and urged them not to relent in their continued support, and briefed the partners on the Federal government's transformation master plan to improve power supply across the country: "When we resumed here, we spent the first three months diagnosing and investigating issues that have affected development in the power sector why the sector is still at the level it is today, and the factors militating against the turnaround that is envisaged in the sector. We consulted, we engaged all the stakeholders. At the end of the diagnosis and investigation, we had a full understanding of the situation.
